text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the description; the position-dependent nature of your vertigo is a key finding. Given your age and hearing changes, do you notice any associated ringing in the ears, tinnitus, or difficulty hearing on one side? Additionally, have you experienced any recent severe headache, double vision, or weakness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The position-dependent nature of your spinning sensation, combined with your age and lack of neurological deficits, is highly characteristic of BPPV. Do you feel any nausea or vomiting during these episodes? REQUEST IMAGES: Dix-Hallpike maneuver video.
